COMPARABILITY VERDICT: this instrument and the earlier round's agree to 2 dp on every normal-vision number I could find (16.59, 25.97, 5.52, 27.34, 28.76, 40.32, L* spacing 2.04 / largest gap 9.26, WCAG 4.79 / 2.03 / 2.44 / 2.84 / 1.48 / 9.14). They differ only on achromatic-bound numbers, and an 8-bit re-quantisation of the simulated grey reproduces the earlier 2.73 (#00004b), 38.37 and 0.34 exactly. So primary (task-defined, unquantised) = 2.76 / 38.26; earlier-round-compatible = 2.73 / 38.37. The CVD model is NOT what separates them: no headline number binds on a CVD condition.

ARTEFACT TO WATCH in (4b): the literal rule 'exclude X itself if it is in the palette' makes #ff00ff the top colour both overall and in the depot hue family (23.14, h_ab 328.2 is within +/-25 deg of the depot's 320.04). #ff00ff is the fire_tracker UAV role colour (serve_dashboard.py:71) - an exact identity with a moving mark, not a free colour. 12 of the 140,608 grid colours are N+ members; lists with them barred are reported alongside and should be the ones used.

STRUCTURAL RESULT: no flat field colour survives achromatic vision against N+ - all 11 named candidates and every top-10 sweep colour have worst-of-5 <= 1.66 dE (most <= 0.44). N+ is even denser in L* than N50. The flag's worst-case legibility therefore comes entirely from the #000000/#ffffff tones (36.90 vs N+, against 38.26 vs N50); the field colour only buys normal-vision hue identity (K7) and extra separation on 21-46 of 126 entries.

DRAW-ORDER DISCREPANCY (code reading, serve_dashboard.py:746-749 then :764): the canvas strokes the 0.18-alpha gridlines BEFORE the 0.22-alpha depot fill, so the real on-gridline pixel inside a depot is depot-over-(gridline-over-ground), not gridline-over-depot as the task worded N+. I built N+ to the task wording for comparability with the second implementer and report the real order as a variant: 125 distinct (grid+depot/BW[10] collapses onto depot/BW[10] = #1a0022), three-tone worst min unchanged at 36.90, candidate normal_min unchanged except #990033 11.78 -> 11.21.

UNMEASURED CAVEAT (derived from code, not rendered): the gridline is lineWidth 0.5 centred on a half-pixel (serve_dashboard.py:746-748: 'ctx.lineWidth=0.5' ... 'Math.round(i*cs)+0.5'), so at devicePixelRatio 1 it covers half of one pixel column and its effective alpha would be about 0.09, not 0.18. The 0.82 gridline composites (mine, the task's, and _sc_deltae.py:81-82's) therefore overstate the darkening at DPR 1 and are exact only at DPR 2. Browser 8-bit alpha rounding (alpha 0.22 -> 56/255) can also shift a composite by 1 LSB; e.g. depot over #124b05 has an exact .5 tie in the green channel (0.78*75 = 58.5), which I resolve half-up.

UNVERIFIABLE: which grey/CVD model the earlier round actually used. Its probe _fov_palette.py lived in a session scratchpad (fovframe_part1.txt:1060-1063) and is not in the repo (Glob outputs/_fov_palette* = no files). The 8-bit-quantisation attribution is inferred from three exact numeric matches; #ff1493's earlier 'worst-case 0.63' matches neither definition (0.60 / 0.72) and remains unexplained.
